Vault Monitor

The Vault Monitor is the internal telemetry system used by to observe pipeline execution and emit structured runtime events for development tools.

During pipeline execution the monitor records lifecycle transitions, stage activity, controller decisions, runtime errors, and other diagnostic signals. These events are normalized into a consistent format and forwarded to the DevTools EventBus, where they can be consumed by debugging tools, analytics utilities, or external DevTools integrations.

The Vault Monitor operates passively and does not influence pipeline execution. It simply observes pipeline activity and produces structured telemetry that can be inspected during development.

Note

Enabling { debug: true } on the main Vault instance is only necessary when the Vault Monitor output is being consumed by the Debugger or a custom EventBus integration. Otherwise the monitor will still emit events, but nothing will be listening to them.

How the Vault Monitor Works

As the Vault pipeline executes, each stage and lifecycle boundary reports activity to the Vault Monitor. The monitor converts these signals into structured EventShape objects describing what occurred during execution.

These events include information such as:

  • Pipeline stage transitions
  • Controller decisions and outcomes
  • Runtime errors and warnings
  • Lifecycle events such as initialization and destruction
  • Optional state snapshots and payload metadata

Once normalized, the events are forwarded to the DevTools EventBus. Development tools such as the built-in debugger, analytics utilities, or browser extensions subscribe to this event stream to observe runtime behavior.

Note

The Vault Monitor only emits events when development mode is active. This ensures that telemetry and debugging instrumentation are available during development while avoiding unnecessary runtime overhead in production environments.

Configuration

Vault emission is active only when development mode is enabled. This ensures that pipeline telemetry is available for diagnostics during development without becoming part of normal production execution behavior.

When development mode is inactive, pipeline events are not emitted through the Event Bus. Consumers may still obtain the singleton instance, but no pipeline event stream will be produced. 

{{`// app.config.ts
export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ 
      devMode: true,
    })
  ]
};`}}
 
{{`Vault({
  devMode: true,
});`}}
 
{{`// main.ts
Vault({
  devMode: true,
});`}}
Vault Monitor Event Model

The Vault Monitor emits structured runtime events describing pipeline activity during Vault execution. These events are normalized into a consistent format and forwarded to the DevTools Event Bus where they can be consumed by debugging tools, analytics utilities, and DevTools integrations.

Rather than documenting individual monitor methods, the event model is defined by three concepts: event categories, event domains, and the event structure. Together these describe how all Vault Monitor telemetry is produced and interpreted.

Each emitted event is assigned a category that determines which fields may appear on the event payload. This policy ensures consistent event structure across the entire pipeline.

Event Categories
Category Description State Payload Error
Boundary Signals transitions in the pipeline lifecycle such as stage start/end, controller decisions, or conductor orchestration events. No Optional No
Error Events representing runtime failures, warnings, or controller exceptions. Required Optional Required
State Events that produce or emit a state snapshot during pipeline execution. Required Optional No

Each event belongs to a domain describing where it originates in the Vault execution engine. The event name combines the domain, phase, and operation.

Event Domains
Domain Description Example Event
Conductor Events describing orchestration decisions made by the Vault conductor, including dispatch, revotes, aborts, and license checks. conductor:start:dispatch
Controller Events emitted during controller evaluation including attempts, votes, successes, failures, and restart decisions. controller:end:vote
Lifecycle Core runtime lifecycle operations including initialization, state emission, error transformation, and internal runtime boundaries. lifecycle:end:initialized
Pipeline Events capturing in-flight candidate values after a pipeline stage completes. Used by DevTools to inspect intermediate state transitions. pipeline:candidate:resolve
Stage Events produced by pipeline processing stages such as resolve, reducer, operator, or filter. stage:start:resolve

All Vault Monitor events follow a consistent structure defined by the EventShape interface. Depending on the event category and configured insight policy, some fields may be omitted from the final emitted event.
